name: arma3_nobe
title: Arma 3
notes: Arma 3 without BattlEye: the game executable directly, the same mission and oracle as arma3.json, the control for the anti-cheat comparison in PAD_BUS_FORK_PLAN.md section 13; anything that differs between the two recipes' runs is BattlEye's doing (2026-09-09: nothing did; launch and readiness are faster without it, 8 s and 18 s against 22 s and 32 s). The oracle is a generated one-soldier mission on the VR world (flat, gridded) whose init.sqf publishes the player's pose through the clipboard about thirty times a second and to the report file a third of a second behind, and reads NIMBUS_RESET and NIMBUS_EXEC commands back from the clipboard (game_harness.py, Arma3Oracle; GAME_TEST_HARNESS.md section 4.3). Yaw and pitch come from getCameraViewDirection: a compass heading, clockwise, so stick right is a positive delta (turn_right_sign 1), pitch up positive; eyeDirection does not follow the aim's pitch. Nothing in SQF sets that pitch, so the reset restores position and yaw (setPosASL, setDir, 0.33 s) and the harness levels the pitch with the right stick at 0.6 (pitch_rate_deg_per_s, about 25 measured). Arma disables a new XInput pad in the player's profile; the oracle sets the engine's Xbox scheme (SchemeMovementLeftBrakeTriggerAccTrigger) behind a .nimbus-harness.bak copy, which only works from the second launch with the pad present. The game keeps a 506x250 start-up window alive beside the real one (window_min_client) and hung when resized while loading (window_stages: ready only; 1280x720 borderless takes at readiness). Walking is about 5 m/s (walk_min_units 2.5), the right-stick deadzone is between 0.30 and 0.40, above the bridge's 0.289 floor (floor_moves_camera false), a full stick turns about 305 deg/s and 0.6 about 36.7. Button A reads as the Action user action (button_echo); Start opens the pause menu, which freezes the mission's script, so nothing presses it. A copy or paste during a run interrupts the pose channel for one read. Measured 2026-09-09 on the pure-Python pad client.

assist.notes: Phase 1 of TARGET_AWARE_AIM_PLAN.md. The mission places the target with NIMBUS_SPAWN at a bearing off where the player is looking and publishes its head through worldToScreen on every pose line; the harness reads that line as a target source and scores the snap in degrees from the same line's bearing. snap_ms is the plan's budget for a target inside the assist radius; wide_snap_ms is for the 30 degree case, which is wider than any shipped tier would engage and takes longer because the gain is set by the dead time. dead_time_pessimism is deliberate: a servo told less than the truth overshoots by about the difference.
